unverified.head_material: cast iron. Explicit: GM 1974 brochure ('Cylinder Head and Block Material: Cast Alloy Iron') and JeepTech ('Block and cylinder heads: cast iron'). Wikipedia only implies it (the 300 switched to iron heads for 1966; 340/350 use the same family of heads). 2 explicit sources.
unverified.firing_order: 1-8-4-3-6-5-7-2 per the 1970 Buick service manual table (TeamBuick reproduction) and TeamBuick tune-up specs - both GM material = 1 source. No independent second/third source reachable (Chilton/Motor scans on Google Books return no snippets; Hot Rod/MotorTrend not fetchable).
unverified.rod_length_in: NHRA blueprints 6.387; Wikipedia 6.385. Only 2 sources, differing in the 3rd decimal.
unverified.compression_by_year: GM brochures: 1968-69 9.0 (2-bbl) / 10.25 (4-bbl); 1970 9.0 / 9.0 / 10.25 (315 hp); 1971-74 8.5 for all. NHRA agrees 1968-70 but prints 10.5 for 1971-74 (probably wrong) and 9.61 for 1976. Over-Drive gives 10.25 for the 280/315 versions. Treat 1968-70 values as solid; 1971-74 8.5 is GM-only.

unverified_variants.found: Over-Drive 1971 fact sheet (260 at 4600) + NHRA (260). GM 1971 brochure: 8.5:1, no hp. Only 2 sources (auction listings excluded).

2-bbl: NHRA 155; Wikipedia 145 (Skylark) and 160 (LeSabre). 4-bbl: NHRA 195; Wikipedia 180 (Skylark 350, single exhaust); Over-Drive implies the dual-exhaust GS 350 at 195 net. GM 1972 brochure gives 8.5:1, no hp. Ratings probably varied by model/exhaust; none reaches 3 sources.
NHRA 190 (Century) + Wikipedia 190. Flory only notes dual exhaust std with Gran Sport, without a figure.

GM 1974 brochure p.56 (350-2 150 @ 3600; 350-4 175 @ 3800; 8.5:1) + NHRA 150/175. Third source not reached (Flory snippets did not return the 1974 chart; Wikipedia says engines carried over from 1973 without figures).
Flory p.674 (350 CID 4-bbl V8 155 X, L77) + NHRA stock guide 155. GM 1979 brochure lists a 5.7 litre 4-bbl V-8, no hp.
Wikipedia says the Buick 350 was built through 1980, but no 1980 Buick-built 350 rating was found. NHRA's 1980 entry (165 hp, LeSabre/Electra) is probably an Oldsmobile 350.

data_check.record: 3.7992 x 3.7992 bore x stroke on a 280 hp Buick 350
data_check.correct: 3.80 in bore x 3.85 in stroke (96.5 x 97.8 mm)
data_check.explanation: 3.7992 in = 96.5 mm, i.e. the bore converted from mm, copied into the stroke as well. 3.7992 x 3.7992 x 8 cyl = 344.6 ci, not 350; 3.80 x 3.85 = 349.3 ci. GM service manual and brochures, NHRA, Wikipedia and JeepTech all give 3.80 x 3.85.

notes: NHRA blueprints BUI-77 and BUI-79 have '350' entries with 4.001 x 3.484 bore/stroke and 5.7 in rods: these are Chevrolet/Oldsmobile 350s fitted to Buicks, not the Buick 350. The NHRA stock guides also mix 160/170 hp Chevy/Olds 350s into 1977-80 Buick listings.
NHRA BUI-75 has no 350 entry; the 1975 NHRA figures come from the NHRA Stock classification guide.
Buick also published 1971 SAE net figures; not collected.
